# Decisions D-1000–D-1249

Part of [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md), which lists every part. Entries keep their order; this part holds the numbers D-1000–D-1249.

<!-- entries -->
- **D-1000 (2026-10-29, the project website: a landing page at the root and the user guide under `/docs`; proposed by
  the landing-page session for the owner's yes in the orchestrator's window; byte class 0, docs and site only).** The
  owner asked for a landing page with downloads, the logo, an interactive demonstration of the desktop app and a
  w3id address, on GitHub Pages beside the MkDocs guide (D-760).
  - **What.** `site/` is the landing page's source: static HTML, CSS and a little JavaScript, self-hosted (no font
    files, no CDN, no analytics, no cookies, no request to another host; a `Content-Security-Policy` meta tag says so).
    MkDocs now builds the guide into `_site/docs` (`site_dir`; `site_url` `…/AgentPROV/docs/`), and
    `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (still `workflow_dispatch` only, D-431) copies `site/` to `_site/` and uploads
    `_site`. `/_site/` replaces `/site/` in `.gitignore`. The guide's header logo leads back to the landing page
    (`extra.homepage`). The design note is `docs/reports/site/design-note.md`.
  - **Content rules.** The page's copy passes the shared claims lint (`claims.lint_text`, as the README and the
    datasheets do) and the O.1.2 phrases it does not cover; the coverage line is the registry-generated phrase; live
    capture is worded as a tested capability with no live results (D-991, U-18). The app tour uses real screenshots of
    v0.1.0 on the synthetic test corpora, taken by `gui/tools/screenshots.py` (light and dark), and describes only what
    user guide chapter 8 documents. Downloads use `github.com/nickjones39/AgentPROV/releases/latest/download/<asset>`
    with the v0.1.0 plan's asset names, including `AgentPROV-0.1.0-source.tar.gz` (F-5). `tests/repo/test_site.py`
    checks all of this, and lists the release-day placeholders (DOIs, the paper and Zenodo links).
  - **w3id.** A patch for `perma-id/w3id.org` (`ids/agentprov/`) adds two rules before the catch-all:
    `w3id.org/agentprov/` and `w3id.org/agentprov/docs/…` redirect to the website; no `/ns` or `/exec` rule changes.
    It is prepared in `docs/reports/site/w3id/` and not submitted: the owner decides when (recommended: release day,
    once the website is live; go-live step 7).
  - **Rejected:** a separate directory name for the landing page with the guide kept at the root (the owner asked for
    the landing page as the address and the guide at `/docs`); a static site generator for one page (a build step and a
    dependency for no gain); a web font (a licence and a file to ship; the platforms' own faces read well and cost
    nothing); embedding a video of the app (large, not accessible, and stale at the next change); taking over the whole
    `w3id.org/agentprov/` catch-all (it would move every non-`/ns` path away from the vocabulary site).
- **D-1001 (2026-10-30, `recompute` rebuilds a sealed corpus's ingest-limit overrides from the recorded source profile,
  accepted only when their digest equals the `aer` stage's recorded `limits_sha256`; approved by the user ("Yes to
  both", in the orchestrator's window) after the wave-2 pre-release checks found it; push pending; byte class 0).**
  D-358 after the wave-2 seal refused `mcphunt-w2b` with `corpus.derive.limits_mismatch`, at its building commit
  `f8b5d62b` and at `c0e711f4` (`docs/reports/release/wave-2-pre-release-checks.md`, check 7). `mcphunt@3` raises
  `max_json_element_bytes` to 64 MiB (D-288, D-323). A working `corpus.json` records the raise under `limits.overrides`,
  but the sealed manifest (`corpus-0.2`, a closed schema) has no `limits` record, so `recompute` replayed the defaults,
  and the importer's D-323 check correctly refused them under the same profile version. The import itself is
  consistent: the limits rebuilt from the profile hash to the recorded `sha256:f4058f07…a2a3`. Only `recompute`'s
  reading of a sealed manifest was missing. A sealed tree of any source whose profile raises a limit would be refused
  the same way.
  - **Decision.** `Derivation.recorded_limit_overrides` keeps `corpus.json`'s `limits` record whenever there is one.
    Without one, it applies the `[import] limits` of the profile that every `aer` stage records (one `id@version` and
    one `limits_sha256` for all of them) to the defaults. It returns their overrides only when
    `sha256(JCS(limits))` equals the recorded `limits_sha256`, and it then adds a notice. In every other case it
    returns no overrides, and the importer's `corpus.derive.limits_mismatch` refusal stands as before: no digest, two
    `aer` stages that disagree, a profile version the package does not ship, or a profile that declares nothing. The
    profile's declaration reaches `corpus/` through a new injected lookup, `Catalogues.profile_limits` (`cli/derive.py`,
    M.5.2(1)), as `worker_caps` does (D-935).
  - **Why the digest.** The recorded `limits_sha256` is the bound fact about what the import ran with. A match proves
    that the rebuilt limits are those limits. The rebuild never picks a value the record does not confirm, so D-323's
    rule against a silent pick holds.
  - **Bytes (class 0).** `corpus/derive.py` and `cli/derive.py` are in no stage scope: all 41 stage digests are identical
    before and after (`tools/r1/stage_digests.py`). Output bytes are unchanged for every corpus that recompute already
    accepted: a working corpus keeps its record, and a sealed corpus with no raised limit rebuilds nothing. Tests:
    `tests/unit/corpus/test_recorded_limits.py` covers:
    - the match case;
    - six mismatch and absent cases;
    - the importer accepting the rebuilt `mcphunt@3` limits and still refusing a mismatch;
    - the CLI lookup.
  - **Rejected.**
    - Option (a) alone, recording `mcphunt`'s D-358 as the pre-seal recompute plus the sealed chain: possible, but the
      fix is narrow, and the same refusal would meet every sealed corpus whose profile raises a limit.
    - Adding a `limits` record to the sealed manifest: `corpus-0.2` is closed and the 43 trees are sealed; a new
      corpus format is class 0 but changes every sealed manifest's bytes.
    - Reading the overrides from the current profile without the digest check: a silent pick, which D-323 forbids.
- **D-1002 (2026-10-30, D-358 after the seal: the re-map rule for units of a withheld neighbour; approved by the user,
  "Approve the rule", in the orchestrator's window, 2026-10-30; a check rule, no code; class 0).** DTap's D-358 after
  its seal exited 1: `exclude_absent` drops withheld objects and RC-13's inputs by sha256, keeps shared objects (RC-14)
  and a withheld execution's own files, so 8 judge files beside a dropped file became outcome-only units, with 121
  register and origins lines about their paths (mapping: `wave-2-pre-release-checks.md`, DTap addendum, and its
  `dtap-d358-mapping/`). **Decision.** A sealed tree passes D-358 when:
  - (i) every execution in both the sealed tree and the recompute is identical, and every sealed-only one is unverified
    for a withheld raw object (H.4.5(6));
  - (ii) every recompute-only execution is an outcome-only unit (`map.no_execution_observed`) whose single primary
    object is in the sealed tree and shares a unit directory with a file the re-map drops on purpose (a withheld object,
    an input only unverified executions use (RC-13), or a withheld execution's primary);
  - (iii) every unexplained `register.jsonl` and `raw/origins.jsonl` line concerns a path instance of such a unit's
    object (select-stage `dedup.collapsed` or `select.not_execution_artefact` rows and their origins rows) or the unit;
  - (iv) the pre-seal recompute at the building commit was identical, and `verify --level chain` passes.

  The mapping is recorded per tree, as for `openagentsafety`'s origins rows: "OK under the D-358 re-map rule, mapping
  recorded". The code fix is a v0.2 roadmap item. **Rejected:** holding DTap on option (a) (the run checks 66,878
  executions and maps every difference); widening the origins-only rule (it would pass unmapped register rows).
- **D-1003 (2026-10-30, `DECISIONS.md` is generated as an index plus parts by decision-number range; approved by the
  user, "yes split it into parts", in the orchestrator's window, 2026-10-30; tooling and docs only; class 0).** With
  D-1002 the generated `DECISIONS.md` reached 1,048,003 bytes, 573 under the 1 MiB limit of
  `tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py`, so the next decision anywhere would have failed it. **Decision.**
  `tools/gen_docs.py` generates a target whose fragment directory holds a `_parts.toml` as an index plus part files.
  `docs/architecture/decisions/_parts.toml` sets 250 decision numbers per part in `docs/architecture/decision-log/`
  (`DECISIONS-0000-0249.md` … `DECISIONS-1000-1249.md`; the first five are 8 KB to 296 KB). An entry goes to the part of
  its number; one without a number stays with the entry before it. Each part keeps the entries' existing order, so
  every entry's text is unchanged. `DECISIONS.md` keeps its path and its preamble (the brief, D0–D12, Addenda A–D) and
  lists the parts in a generated table, so every existing reference to `DECISIONS.md` still resolves.
  `docs/architecture/decisions/` stays the only source. `--check` covers the index and every part, and reports a part
  file that is no longer generated. `--adopt` reads the index and parts back as one text. The merge train's
  decisions resolver also owns `docs/architecture/decision-log/*.md` and stages new part files. `reserve_id.py` scans
  the parts for defined numbers. **Rejected:** a `DECISIONS.md` entry in the test's large-file allowlist (the file keeps
  growing past it); one part per 100 numbers (more files, no gain); parts by date (an entry's place would depend on
  something other than its number); parts next to the spec sections in `docs/architecture/` (`reserve_id.py` scans
  `docs/architecture/*.md` for section headings).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-30, `.gitleaksignore`; user: "i approve Push the decisions-log split, with one allowlist
    line").** Moving entries into the parts gives the D-269 credleak placeholder (accepted as entry 5 under the D-462
    addendum, 2026-10-24) a new path, so gitleaks reports it as a new fingerprint. One commit-pinned line is added for
    it (`db10c3ec…:docs/architecture/decision-log/DECISIONS-0250-0499.md:generic-api-key:258`), making 13 accepted
    entries; `tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py` pins the count.
- **D-1004 (2026-10-30, P-3a: the public repository leaves out every coding-agent file and ignores them; amends D-943's
  P-3 and P-9; the user's decisions of 2026-10-30, relayed by the orchestrator; byte class 0, tools, tests and docs).**
  The user asked: "make sure all AI files, such as claude files and .md files, and any unneeded files are stripped out
  too. making sure to keep the desktop guide and the landing page"; then "do not strip out these files now, we need to
  make a new repo that has been sanitised"; and, on ignoring them, "yes only in the new repo". P-3 had kept
  `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/` and `docs/workflow/` public; this supersedes P-3's "keep" for the agent files.
  - **Decision.** `docs/reports/release/public-export.toml` leaves out, besides P-3's `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/` and
    `docs/mac-studio-handoff.md`: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/`, and what a sweep of the tree found, `docs/review/`
    (the code-review agent's `REVIEW.md` and the ultrareview plan), `tools/review/` (the ultrareview driver) and
    `docs/reports/gui/todo-next-session.md` (a session's to-do brief); plus the user guide's two internal checklists,
    `docs/user-guide/_go-live.md` and `_findings.md` (Q14). Nothing is removed from the development repository, whose
    `.gitignore` is unchanged. Kept: `site/`, `docs/user-guide/` (the desktop app chapters included), `README.md`,
    `LICENSE`, `CITATION.cff`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, the release notes.
  - **The public `.gitignore`.** The export list's new `[gitignore]` table (`reason`, `append`) names patterns that
    `tools/public_export.py export` appends to the public tree's `.gitignore` **in the root commit**, under a comment
    with the reason, so the agent files cannot be committed to the public repository. The equality proof becomes "R
    minus `EXCL`, with `.gitignore` as R's blob plus that block": the expected listing carries the computed blob, and
    `*.export-proof.json` records `gitignore.development_blob`, `public_blob` and `appended`. An appended pattern that
    matches a file the public tree keeps is refused, as is a comment, a negation or a missing reason. The second
    commit (D-980) still changes only `.gitleaksignore`.
  - **The public tree passes its own gate.** `tools/regen_pins.py --check` reused one scratch worktree of the
    development repository, so in another clone (the export) it failed at `git checkout`; a second repository now
    gets its own `regen-pins/repos/<digest>/` worktree and environment. Tests and generators that read the dropped
    files skip when they are absent (`tests/repo/test_repository_hygiene.py` already did for `CLAUDE.md` and
    `.claude/`). `docs/adapter-guide.md`, `pages.yml` and `mkdocs.yml` stop pointing readers at dropped files.
  - **P-9 corrected.** "Pages off" (step 15) contradicted D-1000: the landing page and the MkDocs guide go live on
    GitHub Pages from the public repository, under `https://w3id.org/agentprov/` and `/docs/`, once it is public,
    through the existing manual-dispatch `pages.yml` (D-431 pattern); `public-repo-plan.md` gains step 19.
  - **Rejected:** removing the files from the development repository (the user: "do not strip out these files now");
    the `.gitignore` lines in the development repository too (the user: "only in the new repo"); appending them in the
    second commit (D-980 keeps that commit to `.gitleaksignore`, and the root commit would be the one public commit
    without the guard); a third commit for `.gitignore` alone (the tag would move off the fingerprint commit that the
    D-980 helper tags and checks); deriving the patterns from the
    `[[exclude]]` paths (the fixture and checklist exclusions are not agent files, and the user named agent files).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-30, the user's answer to the open question, relayed by the orchestrator: "Yes to all five:
    push the export prep once green; drop docs/workflow from the export, keep migration and docs/reports; confirm the
    3 sweep finds; add them to the snapshot exclusions and rebuild").** `docs/workflow/` (the multi-session id ledger
    and the session-status schema) leaves the export and joins the public `.gitignore` (`/docs/workflow/`);
    `tools/reserve_id.py` writes no mirror where `.gitignore` ignores it (the reservation stays in the machine
    ledger), and the session-status tests check the schema only where the file is. `migration/` (gate C and the
    migration tests need it) and `docs/reports/` (P-4; `systematic-search/` is cited by the paper by URL) stay. The
    three sweep finds are confirmed; the snapshot list gains them in a separate rebuild (not part of this change).
  - **Byte class 0:** no file here is in a stage digest scope; no AER, SEM or PROV byte, corpus manifest or seal moves.
